questions.q: Fruit colour in squash is an example of :
questions.solution:
Fruit colour in summer squash is the classic case of **dominant epistasis**. The dominant allele W (white) masks the effect of the gene for yellow (Y) and green (yy).

The F2 ratio is **12 white : 3 yellow : 1 green**, a modification of 9:3:3:1.

questions.q: Which one of the following is an example of polygenic inheritance ?
questions.solution:
In **polygenic inheritance** a trait is controlled by several genes with additive effects, producing continuous variation. **Skin colour in humans** is controlled by about three gene pairs, giving many shades.

Pod shape in pea is a single-gene Mendelian trait, Mirabilis flower colour shows incomplete dominance, and male honey bees arise from unfertilised eggs.

questions.q: The phenotypic ratio in the F2 generation of Mendel's dihybrid cross is:
questions.solution:
Crossing round yellow (RRYY) with wrinkled green (rryy) gives round yellow F1 (RrYy). Selfing it gives **9 round yellow : 3 round green : 3 wrinkled yellow : 1 wrinkled green**.

3:1 is the monohybrid phenotypic ratio, 1:2:1 its genotypic ratio, and 1:1:1:1 the dihybrid test-cross ratio.

questions.q: A test cross is a cross between the F1 hybrid and:
questions.solution:
A **test cross** crosses an organism of unknown genotype, such as the F1, with the **homozygous recessive** parent. The recessive parent contributes only recessive alleles, so the offspring show directly which alleles the tested plant carries.

For a monohybrid F1 (Tt × tt) the result is 1:1.

questions.q: In Mirabilis jalapa, the F2 phenotypic ratio for flower colour is:
questions.solution:
Flower colour in Mirabilis jalapa shows **incomplete dominance**: RR red × rr white gives pink Rr in F1.

The F2 is **1 red : 2 pink : 1 white**, so the phenotypic and genotypic ratios are the same, 1:2:1.

questions.q: The F2 ratio 9:7 is characteristic of:
questions.solution:
**Complementary genes** (flower colour in Lathyrus odoratus, Bateson and Punnett) produce colour only when a dominant allele of both genes is present (C_P_). All other combinations are white.

So 9 coloured : 7 white. Dominant epistasis gives 12:3:1, recessive epistasis 9:3:4 and inhibitory genes 13:3.

questions.q: Mendel's law of independent assortment was formulated from the results of:
questions.solution:
Only when two characters are followed together, in a **dihybrid cross**, can one see that the alleles of one gene sort into gametes independently of the other. The new combinations (round green, wrinkled yellow) in F2 show this.

The monohybrid cross gave the laws of dominance and segregation.

questions.q: Plastid (chloroplast) inheritance through leaf variegation in Mirabilis jalapa was first demonstrated by:
questions.solution:
**Carl Correns** (1909) showed that the colour of seedlings in Mirabilis jalapa depends only on the branch that bore the **female** parent flower. Chloroplasts pass through the cytoplasm of the egg, so inheritance is maternal.

Correns was also one of the three rediscoverers of Mendel's work, with de Vries and Tschermak.

questions.q: Mendel's work was rediscovered in the year:
questions.solution:
Mendel published his results in 1865–1866, but they were ignored until **1900**, when **Hugo de Vries, Carl Correns and Erich von Tschermak** independently reached the same conclusions.

1856 is when Mendel began his pea experiments.

questions.q: How many pairs of contrasting characters did Mendel study in the garden pea?
questions.solution:
Mendel studied **seven** pairs: seed shape, seed colour, flower colour, pod shape, pod colour, flower position and stem length.

Pea suited him because it is self-pollinating, has a short life cycle and shows clear contrasting traits.

questions.q: How many different genotypes appear in the F2 of a dihybrid cross (RrYy × RrYy)?
questions.solution:
Each gene gives three genotypes (RR, Rr, rr and YY, Yy, yy). Since they assort independently, the number of combinations is $3 \times 3 = 9$.

The genotypic ratio is 1:2:1:2:4:2:1:2:1.

questions.q: How many phenotypic classes appear in the F2 of a monohybrid cross showing incomplete dominance?
questions.solution:
With incomplete dominance the heterozygote has its own intermediate phenotype, so each genotype is visible: red (RR), pink (Rr), white (rr).

That is **3** classes in a 1:2:1 ratio, against 2 classes under complete dominance.

questions.q: In dominant epistasis for fruit colour in summer squash, how many of the 16 F2 combinations give white fruit?
questions.solution:
Any plant with at least one dominant W is white, whatever the other gene: W_Y_ (9) plus W_yy (3) gives **12**.

The remaining 3 (wwY_) are yellow and 1 (wwyy) green: 12:3:1.

questions.q: Kernel colour in wheat is controlled by three gene pairs with additive effect. How many phenotypic classes appear in the F2?
questions.solution:
With n gene pairs the number of phenotypic classes is $2n + 1$, since a plant may carry 0 to 2n dominant (colour) alleles.

For n = 3: $2(3) + 1 = 7$, distributed 1:6:15:20:15:6:1 out of 64 (Nilsson-Ehle).

questions.q: Explain the incomplete dominance with example.
questions.solution:
**Incomplete dominance** is the condition in which neither allele is completely dominant over the other, so the heterozygote shows a phenotype **intermediate** between the two parents. It was described by Carl Correns.

**Example: flower colour in Mirabilis jalapa (4 o'clock plant).** Red (RR) × white (rr): all F1 plants are **pink** (Rr). Selfing the F1 (Rr × Rr) gives F2 RR : Rr : rr = **1 red : 2 pink : 1 white**.

Points to note:
1. The phenotypic and genotypic ratios are both 1:2:1.
2. Parental phenotypes reappear in F2, so the genes did not blend; they segregated unchanged. This supports particulate inheritance.
3. The red allele makes only enough pigment in a single dose to give pink.

Another example is Antirrhinum (snapdragon) flower colour.
